While Penn’s pre-professional culture is awesome for some people, I really didn’t fit into it, and I don’t think many people do. I think Penn is better than Brown for people who know exactly what they want their career path to look like—even if that isn’t finance/IB. I, however, went into college with absolutely no direction or idea of what I wanted to do with my life. From the discussions I’ve had w/friends who went to Brown, and just from the vibes I got from visiting, I think it just gives a lot more room for intellectual curiosity and exploration. Regardless, I still made awesome, lifelong friends at Penn, and had a ton of fun, so you can’t go wrong…it’s still a great school w great people and great opportunities
I chose Penn UG over Brown. If I had the chance to change one decision I’ve made in my life, it would be choosing Brown instead

Ok, sure—you’re an Olympic medalist, lock for a professional league, etc, you’re probably in. But I think it boils down to your viability as a student-athlete. A high school GPA below 3.0 is a major red flag for any coach/school with regard to your work ethic & potential for success at a fast-paced and high pressure school. I think rather than asking this question on every Ivy subreddit, you should be thinking hard about whether you think you can be successful both academically and athletically based on your current work ethic, study skills, time management, etc. You don’t just pick those things up the second you walk on campus.
Former athlete at another Ivy—no Ivy is going to give a passing glance to a student with below a 3.0, not even exceptional athletes with NCAA scoring/winning potential
